summary.headline: Sammaan Capital Q2 FY27 PAT rose about 28% QoQ to INR312 crore, with disbursements up 62% QoQ to INR6,278 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed higher disbursements, lower gross NPA (0.15%) and PAT of INR312 crore against INR243 crore in Q1. AUM rose to INR59,188 crore from INR56,239 crore. IHC converted the first warrant tranche (INR906 crore, promoter stake 28.34% to 33.32%) and the remaining INR2,291 crore is due by September 2027. Management said cost of funds is falling, though it flagged a rising rate environment, and reiterated full-year targets. The call was also used to introduce new leaders and describe governance changes.

segments.name: Mortgages (residential, affordable, LAP-type)
segments.commentary: Residential housing finance about INR31,445 crore of AUM. More than 3,600 staff dedicated to mortgages; the company has sold down about INR108,000 crore of mortgage pools to 24 partners, with 90+ day delinquency below 0.5%.

segments.name: Secured business loans and home loan equity
Commercial real estate, project, plot and lease rental discounting
segments.commentary: About INR11,118 crore of AUM, with lending through credit funds and portfolio purchases.

segments.name: Other loans (unsecured business, working capital, personal)
segments.commentary: About INR1,543 crore of AUM. Personal loans are moving from pool purchases to own origination through 20 branches, targeting about INR2 lakh tickets and 16-17% yield on purchased books.

segments.name: Loan against securities
segments.commentary: About INR270 crore of AUM; personal loan against securities initiated or expanded in H1.

segments.name: Gold loans (new)
segments.commentary: Policies approved; soft launch in about 16 branches in Q3 FY27, 30 more branches in Q4, wider rollout in FY28. Indicative ticket about INR2 lakh, yield 11-13%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM target about INR70,700 crore (against INR59,188 crore at Q2); loan book target INR53,000 crore (INR46,482 crore at Q2).
FY27 disbursement ambition INR30,100 crore; H1 disbursement of INR10,123 crore met the INR10,000 crore guidance, and H2 requires about INR20,000 crore.
FY27 PAT target INR1,400 crore; H1 PAT was INR556 crore.
Branch network to rise from 245 to about 300 by year-end FY27.
Guided margin of around 3.5%; management expects net interest income and margins to expand steadily.
Cost of funds target 9.3%, though management is mindful of the rate environment. The whole book was repriced up 25 bps from November 2026.

Target borrowing mix: about 60% rupee term loans and bonds (30% each), about 20% assignments, pass-through certificates and co-lending, and 20% foreign currency (10-15% dollar bonds, 5-10% dollar loans).
Long-term aim is AAA rating (currently AA+) with ROMA above 2%; management said a competitive ROE is expected over the next four to six quarters.
Auditor rotation next year; the company is in talks with large audit firms.
capex_capacity: Branches up from 217 to 245 across 20 states in Q2; target about 300 by year-end FY27.
More than 1,000 employees added in H1 (1,123 hires, 1,072 for retail franchise); on-roll manpower above 4,500 at end-September, with about 250 further offers accepted.
Salesforce LOS live in more than 20 branches, with countrywide rollout planned in Q3 FY27. Salesforce CRM with 2,418 users and more than 2.09 lakh leads since June 2026.
Over 12 IT projects implemented June-October; 53 AI use cases identified, 35 targeted for FY27. A separate AI and technology centre of excellence is being set up.
Core loan management system under upgrade.
demand_pricing: Management says the NBFC retail credit market (housing, personal and gold loans) will grow from INR26 trillion in FY26 to INR37 trillion by FY28, with core segments of INR17 trillion to INR24 trillion. The company aims for a 2% market share.
About 94% of Q2 disbursements were secured.

Fee income fell to INR33 crore from INR59 crore in Q1, and derecognition gain was INR7 crore. Ramnath Shenoy attributed this to bank rates rising and spreads being squeezed; management expects the line to expand over two to three quarters after the 1 November rate increase.
Rising rates: management says the company's absolute coupon is still falling, even with a hypothetical 100 bps repo hike, and it is focused on spreads per loan.
Competition: management says peers with larger balance sheets would see coupons rise in absolute terms.
UAE bank support: one large UAE bank in the IHC group extended over USD150 million at competitive rates, and a second is expected to do a similar-size transaction in the next couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: How will rising rates affect margins and loan growth over the next 12-18 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Gagan Banga said bank rate transmission has started, and the company's percentage coupon will keep falling even with a hypothetical 100 bps hike. The whole book was repriced up 25 bps from November, so spreads may expand in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: How do increased branch and headcount costs reconcile with the PAT growth plans, and what is the UAE bank relationship?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Chaudhary said mortgage branches break even in about six months, personal and business loan branches in four to six months, and gold branches in 12-18 months. Gagan Banga said a UAE bank already provided over USD150 million and a second is expected to do a similar deal in the next couple of months, lowering cost of funds.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the stock not re-rated, with price-to-book still below 1x?
qa_highlights.answer: Gagan Banga said a declining cost of funds and rating upgrades typically lift the price-to-book multiple with a lag. He expects re-rating from operating performance and the AAA target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding plan and optimal debt mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Gagan Banga said the target mix is about 60% rupee term loans and bonds, 20% assignments and pass-through certificates, and 20% dollar bonds and loans. Asset maturity is about three to four years, and ALM matching is critical.

qa_highlights.question: Are fee income and securitisation guidance on track, and is the 30% securitisation target intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramnath Shenoy said upfront fee income depends on sold-down stock and floating spreads, and spreads were squeezed this quarter. Gagan Banga said the line should expand over two to three quarters. The call did not give a clear answer on the 30% securitisation target.

qa_highlights.question: Who succeeds the Interim Chairman, and what is the auditor status?
qa_highlights.answer: Gagan Banga said a chairperson will be appointed shortly, with new independent directors to follow. Auditor rotation is due next year, and the company is engaged with large audit firms. BDO is already co-sourced for internal audit.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to reach a majority stake, and are FY27 targets intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Gagan Banga said the company is well capitalised and the business does not need capital. IHC can convert warrants until September 2027. He said FY27 disbursement and profit targets are all intact.

risks_watch: Rising rates: cost of funds of 9.8% must fall to the 9.3% target while lenders pass through hikes; the 25 bps repricing and the spread squeeze on sold-down books need to be watched.
H2 execution: disbursements must rise from INR10,123 crore in H1 to about INR20,000 crore in H2, with PAT of INR1,400 crore for FY27 against INR556 crore in H1.
Cost-to-income is a stated focus area; headcount and branch expansion (245 to about 300) and the gold loan launch add operating cost before revenue.
Fee and derecognition income fell sharply in Q2; the 30% securitisation target was not clearly confirmed.
Board and governance transition: interim chairman exits 22 November 2026; chairperson and independent director appointments and the statutory auditor rotation next year are pending.
Remaining warrant conversion of INR2,291 crore by September 2027; book value per share would move from INR162.6 to INR153.9 on conversion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, liquidity and the cost of funds trajectory, and clearly focused on governance and the AAA goal. Less specific on the fee and securitisation line, where the answer was that income will fluctuate, and on the source of the stock's low price-to-book.
key_quotes: Our focus is on building these credentials through execution rather than pursuing growth at the expense of quality.
The business per se is not in need of capital.
Our percentage coupon will be falling.
We are more focused on the spread that we earn per loan, and that I think sanity will continue to remain in the marketplace and the spreads will be maintained.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branches are rising from 245 to about 300 by year-end FY27 across 20 states (22.4% more), with branch openings already under way from 217 in Q1 to 245 in Q2.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 targets (PAT INR1,400 crore against INR556 crore in H1) rather than raising them, and the H2 step-up is steep.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 needs about INR20,000 crore of disbursements and about INR844 crore of PAT (INR1,400 crore less INR556 crore), against a rising rate environment, fee income down to INR33 crore from INR59 crore, and a 9.8% cost of funds still to reach 9.3%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q3 FY27 soft launch; Q4 FY27 expansion
rows.why: Gold loans have approved policies with a soft launch in about 16 branches in Q3 FY27 and 30 more in Q4, with wider rollout in FY28 at about INR2 lakh tickets and 11-13% yield.

rows.label: Branch breakeven and headcount build
rows.why: Mortgage branches break even in about six months, personal and business loan branches in four to six months and gold branches in 12-18 months, while on-roll manpower is above 4,500 with about 250 more offers accepted, so operating cost leads revenue in the window.

rows.label: UAE bank funding support lowers cost of funds
rows.why: One UAE bank in the IHC group extended over USD150 million at competitive rates and a second is expected to do a similar-size deal, which supports the drive from 9.8% toward the 9.3% cost of funds target.

rows.label: Remaining IHC warrant conversion of INR2,291 crore
rows.why: The first tranche of INR906 crore converted, lifting promoter stake from 28.34% to 33.32%, and the remaining INR2,291 crore is due by September 2027, which would dilute book value per share from INR162.6 to INR153.9.

tone.note: Management was confident on disbursement and PAT targets, cost of funds trajectory and the AAA goal, but was less specific on fee income and the 30% securitisation target, and did not explain the low price-to-book; analysts pressed on rising-rate spreads and the H2 step-up.

oneOffs.what: Fee income fell to INR33 crore from INR59 crore in Q1, with derecognition gain of INR7 crore; this weakens the non-interest line rather than lifting growth

quality.why: Growth is driven by volume: disbursements rose 62% QoQ to INR6,278 crore and AUM grew from INR56,239 crore to INR59,188 crore (about 5% QoQ), with no acquisition or exceptional gain in the brief. However, the brief compares QoQ, not YoY, and the fee line fell sharply, and management expects spreads to stay squeezed by the 25 bps repricing and rising rates.
